sample_unit: patients (TCGA glioma dataset; count not reported in text)

links.outcome: Fairness metrics and prediction performance after reweighting and equalized-odds mitigation across race and gender groups
links.effect: For race, reweighting with logistic regression worsened outcomes for the under-represented group and increased unfairness, while equalized-odds post-processing improved results for the under-represented group and significantly improved fairness.
links.quote: For the most severe bias (race), the pre-trained logistic regression model using the reweighting algorithm shows some deterioration in prediction outcomes for the under-represented group and even an increase in unfairness, while the post-processing approach improves results for the under-represented group and provides significant improvements in fairness.

links.outcome: Performance and fairness disparities by race and gender in glioma grade prediction
links.effect: Demographic bias, most severe for race, was found in glioma grading classifiers; disparate impact, equal opportunity difference and error rate difference were evaluated by group.
links.quote: For the most severe bias (race), the pre-trained logistic regression model using the reweighting algorithm shows some deterioration in prediction outcomes for the under-represented group and even an increase in unfairness, while the post-processing approach improves results for the under-represented group and provides significant improvements in fairness.

screen.practice: bias mitigation (reweighting and equalized odds post-processing)
screen.reason: Empirically tests and compares fairness mitigation practices (pre-processing reweighting vs post-processing equalized odds) to evaluate demographic fairness and performance tradeoffs in glioma grade prediction.

primary.practice: algorithmic bias mitigation techniques (reweighting and equalized odds post-processing)
